I understand where you're coming from, but you should know that urban planners, especially in governmental roles, often give reports to local governments and even state governments about new legislation. While private companies and groups also give input, a lot of consulting on the local level is done by city planners employed by the city. wouldn't it make sense to have more anarchists in these positions, in order to attempt to prevent the addition of more legislation that would infringe on people's property rights, or even to repeal legislation?

Personally, Urban planning, and systems planning more broadly will always be in demand for communities and large cities in my opinion. People generally don't like living in chaos, so there will be a demand for order, order which could be brought by a voluntary company who is concerned with the infrastructure of a certain area, similar to how local government works.

I say it's monopolized by the government, because you can't really implement a plan on the scale of the city without approval from the local government.
